origin.description: Computes the lagged and iterated differences.
origin.usage: diff2(x, idxs = NULL, lag = 1L, differences = 1L, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length N.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: An integer specifying the order of difference.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If NA, the default behavior of the function about naming support is remained. If FALSE, no naming support is done. Else if TRUE, names attributes of result are set.

origin.details: Computes the lagged and iterated differences. The implementation subsets with the matrixStats index rules, then subtracts elements lag steps apart, repeating that subtraction differences times.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length N - differences.

translation.description: Computes the lagged and iterated differences.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A one-dimensional numeric vector of length N. Integer and floating values are computed as float64.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A 1-based index vector, or a logical mask, selecting the elements to operate over. None selects every element. Positive indexes past the vector and missing indexes become missing values. Negative indexes drop positions. Zero is ignored.

arguments.name: lag
arguments.text: Lag, as a positive integer. The default is 1. A non-integer is truncated toward zero, as R's as.integer does.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: Order of difference, as a positive integer. The default is 1. A non-integer is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: This is useNames in R. TRUE or FALSE is accepted. Names are not attached to the result; the numeric values are the result that is checked.

translation.details: Computes the lagged and iterated differences. Subsetting and the difference loop are the Rust crate diff2, ported from matrixStats src/diff2.c and the index rules that function calls. The result is always a one-dimensional float64 array.
translation.value: A one-dimensional float64 array. Its length is the number of selected elements minus differences times lag, or zero when that quantity is negative.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.diff2 import diff2

diff2(np.arange(1, 11))
